goal: Restore independent-key progress for cachetools cached/cachedmethod with condition set (info on and off) while preserving same-key stampede suppression, hit/miss accounting, exception cleanup and public behavior; python3 run_checks.py must pass (task tests + upstream + agent_tests).

note: Reproduced D1: all 8 subtests of benchmark_tests.test_independent_keys_and_cached_hits fail; upstream 338 pass. Discriminating evidence (TMPDIR scratch): lock is acquirable while held call runs and cache has no eviction pressure (0-1/128), yet the unrelated caller is parked in Condition.wait_for on the global predicate 'not pending' at src/cachetools/_cached.py:24,153 and _cachedmethod.py:165,279. Fixed predicate to wait only for the caller's own key. Added agent_tests/test_independent_key_progress.py (4 tests) which fails on pre-fix source (independent-key + concurrency tests) and passes after.
risk: Pre-existing, out-of-scope limitation confirmed but not changed: with a real threading.Condition plus a distinct lock= object, notify_all() is called without holding the condition's lock (upstream tests only use mock lock/condition). Regression tests use short (0.3s) observation windows for suppression, which is directional: they cannot false-fail on a correct implementation, but an extremely slow machine could miss a broken one.
summary: Restored independent-key progress for condition-based caching: the wait predicate in src/cachetools/_cached.py (_condition_info/_condition) and src/cachetools/_cachedmethod.py (_condition_info/_condition) now waits only for the caller's own cache key (k not in pending) instead of any pending computation. Added agent_tests/test_independent_key_progress.py (4 tests, 16 subTest cases) covering decorator x info x hot-key progress, distinct-key concurrency, same-key stampede suppression with hit/miss accounting, and same-key recovery after a failed computation.
